--- title: "Player impact from lineups" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} ## Takeaways - **Lineups rebuilt for every game since 2003-04 (NBA) and 2009 (WNBA).** In every season they account for at least 95% of points and possessions (98-100% in most). - **Player impact predicts next season better than the team's own results.** Last season's player impact, weighted by who actually plays this season, explains 50% of next-season NBA team net rating (36% WNBA), against 35% (24% WNBA) for the team's own net rating last season. - **Adding player impact to net rating predicts playoff series better.** Over 210 NBA series, adding impact from players available for the playoffs beats net rating alone (one-sided p = 0.03; the 95% interval just touches zero). In the WNBA (62 series) the gain points the same way but is not significant. - **Weighting the archetype mix by player quality did not beat quality alone.** Who is good matters more than which role they play. ::: ## How it is measured Every stretch of play with the same ten players on the floor (a *stint*) is one observation. A ridge regression gives each player an **offense** and a **defense** effect in points per 100 possessions, holding the other nine players fixed. The ridge penalty pulls small samples toward average, and each season starts from the player's previous-season estimate. Defense counts as much as offense here, unlike box-score measures. **Avoiding leakage:** this season's impact, summed across a roster, rebuilds this season's net rating. So every roster-based prediction below uses **last season's** player impact applied to this season's roster. ## Top players (latest two seasons) At least 800 minutes.
